text:
Olivia Chen: hey team :wave: I followed the k8s onboarding doc but I don't see our staging namespace in my kubectl contexts. `kubectl config get-contexts` only shows 'redwood-dev' and 'redwood-prod'. I'm on mac (M1). Did I miss a step?

DevEx Bot: welcome Olivia! tagging @Sam Kim from infra. quick checks: did you run the cloud provider kubeconfig update step from the doc? also check `echo $KUBECONFIG` and `kubectl config get-contexts -o name` to confirm what's merged.

Sam Kim: hey Olivia — staging cluster is `redwood-staging-us-west-2`. Two quick possibilities:
1) your kubeconfig didn't get merged (common with multiple kubeconfig files)
2) you're using an SSO/profile that hasn't fetched staging creds yet.
Can you paste output of `kubectl config get-contexts -o name` and `echo $KUBECONFIG`?

Olivia Chen: sure — output below:
```
$ kubectl config get-contexts -o name
redwood-dev
redwood-prod
```
`$ echo $KUBECONFIG`
`/Users/olivia/.kube/config:/Users/olivia/.kube/config-aws`

Olivia Chen: also when I try `kubectl get ns` I get a few namespaces but not staging.

Priya Rao: hey! looks like you have multiple kubeconfig files joined by colon — the staging context is in the AWS-generated file (`config-aws`) but the merged order can hide it. try `KUBECONFIG=/Users/olivia/.kube/config-aws kubectl config get-contexts -o name` to check. If that shows `redwood-staging-us-west-2` then merge it with `kubectl config view --flatten > ~/.kube/merged-config` and then `export KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/merged-config` or replace your main `~/.kube/config` after backing up.

Sam Kim: also if you use AWS SSO, run `aws sso login --profile redwood` first, then re-run `aws eks update-kubeconfig --name redwood-staging --region us-west-2 --profile redwood`. If the context appears but `kubectl get pods -n staging` returns forbidden, you'll need a namespace rolebinding.

Olivia Chen: running that now... `aws sso login` asked for browser auth and then `update-kubeconfig` added `redwood-staging-us-west-2` — thanks! But when I `kubectl get pods -n staging` I get `Error from server (Forbidden): pods is forbidden: User "arn:aws:iam::1234567890:role/Redwood-SSO-Redwood" cannot list resource "pods" in API group "" in the namespace "staging"`

Priya Rao: that means your IAM->k8s RBAC mapping doesn't include the namespace rolebinding. Sam can create a short-lived RoleBinding to give you view access.

Sam Kim: @Olivia can you DM me your company email (or paste here if you're comfortable) so I can create the RoleBinding? I'll give you `view` on `staging` for now.

Olivia Chen: olivia.chen@redwood.example.com — thanks!

Sam Kim: done — created RoleBinding `rb-olivia-staging-view` in `staging` and bound to `kubernetes.io/group: redwood-engineers` and your principal. Try `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n staging` and then `kubectl get pods -n staging`.

Olivia Chen: `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n staging` -> `yes` 
`kubectl get pods -n staging` now shows pods. :tada:

Olivia Chen: huge thanks everyone, that fixed it. I'll update my notes for future new hires (and maybe suggest adding a small troubleshooting FAQ in the onboarding doc).

Priya Rao: great — pls add a note about `KUBECONFIG` ordering and the SSO step. saved a bunch of time. :+1:

DevEx Bot: added a pointer to the onboarding doc for `KUBECONFIG` issues and `aws sso` in the next doc PR — thanks for flagging!
